clue.text: Very hot grease swallowed by singer

indicators.note: being swallowed by something puts the grease inside the singer's name

parts.note: Bing Crosby, the American crooner
oil is a lubricating grease

explanation.surface: Scalding fat gulped down by a performer.
explanation.definitionFit: Water at its bubbling point is the stock image of extreme heat, so the word means scorching.

clue.text: Dishonest man gets rotten potatoes

parts.note: rotten food has gone bad
mash is mashed potato

explanation.surface: A crook is served spoiled spuds.
explanation.definitionFit: Badmash is an Anglo-Indian word for a hooligan or rogue, a man of bad character.

clue.text: Fashionable underwear producing funds

parts.note: in means in fashion
vests are undershirts in British English

explanation.surface: Trendy undergarments bringing in money.
explanation.definitionFit: To fund something is to put money into it, as an investor does; both are verbs here.

clue.text: Former king of Libya is here, so I'd nearly stand up

parts.note: taken as written, without the apostrophe

indicators.note: nearly means almost all of it, so the last letter goes

parts.note: to stand up is to rise

explanation.surface: A deposed monarch says his presence makes the speaker almost get to their feet.
explanation.definitionFit: Idris I ruled Libya from 1951 until Gaddafi's coup in 1969.

clue.text: Re-reading this word upset a soldier

indicators.note: upset means knocked over, so the letters of re-reading are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: Reading a word again bothers a soldier.
explanation.definitionFit: Grenadiers are infantry soldiers, originally those who threw grenades, as in the Grenadier Guards.

clue.text: Occasional workers might wear these

definitions.meaning: temporary staff hired on an irregular basis
informal clothes or shoes, the sort people wear off duty

explanation.surface: Part-time staff and the clothes they might turn up in.
explanation.definitionFit: Temporary hires are casual workers, and relaxed everyday clothing goes by the same plural noun.

clue.text: Talk about the end of confidence trickster

indicators.note: talk goes about, or around, the other letter

parts.note: to chat is to talk

indicators.note: the end of the word confidence is its final letter

explanation.surface: A conversation about how a con artist works.
explanation.walkthrough: 'confidence trickster' reads as one phrase, but 'confidence' only supplies its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A swindler who deceives people for gain is a cheat.

clue.text: Cartoon character is great, when attracting her love

parts.note: super means great or excellent
love is zero in tennis, the letter O

explanation.surface: A comic-strip figure is splendid when he wins a woman's love.
explanation.definitionFit: Batman and Superman are caped crusaders who star in comic and cartoon strips.

clue.text: To be sick confines girl to such correspondence

indicators.note: to confine is to enclose, so the sickness word holds the girl inside

parts.note: to ail is to be ill
Irma is a girl's name

explanation.surface: Illness keeps a young woman indoors, writing letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Letters sent by plane are posted as overseas air post, a kind of correspondence.

clue.text: Lengthen a prison sentence

definitions.meaning: to pull something longer, a verb
slang for a period served in jail

explanation.definitionFit: Pulling something longer is stretching it, and slang calls a spell in jail a stretch.

clue.text: Poet turns to take semi-fierce part

indicators.note: the poet's name turns round, read from its end

parts.note: Ovid, the Roman poet

indicators.note: semi means half, here the back half of the word fierce

explanation.surface: A poet changing direction to play a rather fierce role.
explanation.walkthrough: 'semi-fierce' gives the second half of FIERCE, RCE. 'part' is a verb here, as in to separate.
explanation.definitionFit: To part as a couple, or separate legally, is to end a marriage.

clue.text: A purple butterfly is yours for a sovereign

definitions.meaning: the Purple ... is a large British butterfly
a supreme ruler, such as the head of an empire

explanation.surface: Offering someone a purple butterfly in exchange for a gold coin.
explanation.definitionFit: A monarch ruling an empire is a sovereign, and the Purple Emperor butterfly carries the same title.

clue.text: He'll help a simpleton to sit around getting 1 No Trump

parts.note: an ass is a foolish person

indicators.note: around suggests the letters of sit being moved about

parts.note: one is written as the letter A, as in a single thing
NT is the bridge abbreviation for a no-trump bid

explanation.surface: A fool at the bridge table sits about and bids one no-trump.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' is the anagram signal for sit. In bridge, a bid of 1NT means one no trumps, so '1 No Trump' gives A and NT.
explanation.definitionFit: A helper or aide is someone whose job is giving help.

clue.text: Aggressively criticise a Sunday meal?

definitions.meaning: to slate someone harshly, a verb
the traditional British Sunday lunch of cooked joint of meat

explanation.definitionFit: To lay into someone harshly is to roast them, and the British Sunday lunch of baked meat is a roast.

clue.text: Hurry! Don't start to get nun-like

indicators.note: do not begin, so the opening letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: nuns take a vow of chastity, so nun-like means chaste

explanation.surface: An urgent warning not to begin behaving like a nun.
explanation.definitionFit: Speed or urgency is the noun sense of hurry, as in more haste, less speed.

clue.text: Listener bruised and put aside

parts.note: an ear is the organ that listens
bruised skin is marked

explanation.surface: Someone who listened got hurt and was pushed to one side.
explanation.definitionFit: Reserving something for a particular purpose, as with funds, is setting it aside.

clue.text: Grotty toast leads to sickness

parts.note: British slang for unwell or rotten, so ill
a toast is drunk to someone's health

explanation.surface: A disgusting slice of toast making someone sick.
explanation.walkthrough: 'toast' misleads as bread; it is the toast drunk at a party, 'your health'.
explanation.definitionFit: Poor physical condition or being unwell is a state of sickness.

clue.text: It may win or lose a bridge contract, but it might wake everybody up

definitions.text: It may win or lose a bridge contract
definitions.meaning: the final trump card held in a hand of bridge can decide the contract
in Christian belief a final trumpet blast will wake the dead on Judgement Day

explanation.definitionFit: The final trump card can decide a bridge hand, and the trumpet call of Judgement Day raises the dead.

clue.text: Deodorant might be needed here, when ready for a fight

definitions.meaning: the armpits, where deodorant is applied

explanation.definitionFit: Armpits are where deodorant goes, and soldiers equipped for battle are said to be under arms.

clue.text: Ill-omened, unlike a Kingsley Amis character?

parts.note: the prefix un- makes something unlike, or the opposite of, what follows
Lucky Jim is the title character of Kingsley Amis's 1954 comic novel

explanation.surface: An ill-fated figure who is nothing like a hero from an Amis novel.
explanation.definitionFit: Something ill-omened promises bad fortune, which is the meaning of jinxed or ill-starred.

clue.text: A cricket captain may do so and confess

definitions.text: A cricket captain may do so
definitions.meaning: in cricket the batting captain may end his side's innings early

explanation.definitionFit: A cricket captain ends his side's innings early by declaring, and to own up is to declare openly.

clue.text: Unusual topic related to the eye

indicators.note: unusual signals that the word topic appears in an unfamiliar arrangement

explanation.surface: An odd subject concerning eyesight.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describes anything connected with sight or the eye, as in the optic nerve.

clue.text: Drinking vessel for a circus entertainer

definitions.meaning: a flat-bottomed glass without a stem

explanation.definitionFit: A stemless glass for drinking is a tumbler, and so is an acrobat who turns somersaults in the ring.

clue.text: Musical instrument contains nothing of use to lesser royalty

indicators.note: the instrument holds the other letter within it

parts.note: a cornet is a brass instrument like a small trumpet
nothing is zero, the letter O

explanation.surface: A brass instrument with nothing in it that a minor royal could use.
explanation.definitionFit: A small crown worn by peers and minor royals rather than by monarchs is a coronet.

clue.text: Small sailing vessel off-loads iron to get to a town in Italy

indicators.note: unloading cargo takes it off, so the iron is removed from the boat's name

parts.note: a felucca is a small Mediterranean sailing boat
Fe is the chemical symbol for iron

explanation.surface: A little boat unloads its iron cargo to reach an Italian port.
explanation.definitionFit: Lucca is a walled Tuscan city in central Italy, the birthplace of Puccini.

clue.text: I'm behind schedule for La Mer, which includes wild brief love etc

indicators.note: La Mer contains the other pieces inside it

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: wild suggests the letters of etc running out of order

parts.note: love is zero in tennis scoring, written in short as the single letter O

explanation.surface: Someone arriving late for a performance of Debussy's La Mer.
explanation.walkthrough: La Mer is Debussy's orchestral work about the sea; here it is just letters to be split around the inserted pieces, with 'wild' scrambling etc.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone arriving after the start is a person running late, who could say they are behind schedule.

clue.text: Tempted evangelist half wanting to take wine

indicators.note: half of the word is missing, so its second pair of letters goes

parts.note: Luke is one of the four Gospel writers
red is red wine

explanation.surface: A preacher partly giving in to the temptation of drink.
explanation.definitionFit: To entice or draw someone in with bait is to tempt them; both are past tense.

clue.text: Group of people, actors at the end of a farce

parts.note: the actors in a play are its cast

indicators.note: the final letter of the word farce

explanation.surface: Players taking a bow when a farce finishes.
explanation.definitionFit: A hereditary social class, especially in the Hindu system, is a closed group of people.

clue.text: Attractive woman offers a biscuit

definitions.meaning: British slang for a stunning woman
a thin crisp savoury biscuit, often eaten with cheese

explanation.surface: A pretty woman handing round a biscuit.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang calls a stunner a cracker, and a crisp savoury wafer eaten with cheese is also one.

clue.text: No lisp by upper class turns into a Greek letter

parts.note: U is the old British label for upper-class usage

indicators.note: the letters of no lisp are changed into a new form

explanation.surface: A posh speaker losing a lisp turning into Greek.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turns into' rearranges NOLISP to PSILON; U, the old label for posh speech, comes first.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the twentieth character of the Greek alphabet, the source of the letter Y.

clue.text: Having submitted could have made Eddy lie

indicators.note: the words Eddy lie could be rearranged to make the answer

explanation.surface: Giving in might have forced Eddy to tell a falsehood.
explanation.definitionFit: To give way or surrender is to yield, so the past tense means having given in.

clue.text: Pantomime character wants mole to perish

parts.note: a mole is a stone breakwater or jetty, so a pier
to perish is to decay or rot

explanation.surface: A panto clown hoping a burrowing animal will die.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mole' is not the animal but a harbour wall.
explanation.definitionFit: Pierrot is the sad white-faced clown figure from French pantomime and commedia.
